title: Subsets Whose Min Plus Max Fits
statement:
You get an array nums and an integer target. Count the non-empty subsequences whose smallest element plus largest element is at most target.

Subsequences are chosen by index, so equal values at different positions make different subsequences. A one-element subsequence uses that element as both its minimum and its maximum.

The count can be huge: return it modulo 1 000 000 007.

examples.why: With 1 as the minimum, any of 3, 4, 6 may join (1 + 6 = 7 fits): 2³ = 8 choices. With 3 as the minimum, only 4 may join: 2 more. A lone 4 fails since 4 + 4 = 8.
Even a single 5 counts as min and max: 5 + 5 = 10 is too big.
Every non-empty choice of the three positions works: 2³ − 1 = 7. Counting distinct values would give 1.

hints: Only the minimum and the maximum of a subsequence matter. Does the original order of nums matter at all?
Sort the array. If you fix the minimum at index i and the largest allowed value ends at index j, how many subsequences have nums[i] as their minimum?
Each element between i and j can be in or out: 2^(j − i) choices. Two pointers find j for every i as i moves right, because j can only move left.

explain.intuition:
A subsequence is just a set of positions, and the condition only looks at its smallest and largest value, so you may sort first. After sorting, fix the leftmost chosen index i as the minimum. The other chosen elements may be any subset of indexes i+1 … j, where j is the last index with nums[i] + nums[j] ≤ target. That is 2^(j−i) subsets, the empty one meaning "just nums[i]".

As i moves right the minimum grows, so the allowed j can only shrink. That is the classic two-pointer shape: a left pointer for the minimum and a right pointer that only ever moves left.
steps: Sort nums and precompute pow2[k] = 2^k mod 1e9+7 for k up to n.
While lo <= hi: if nums[lo] + nums[hi] ≤ target, add pow2[hi − lo] and move lo right; otherwise move hi left.
pitfalls: Using lo < hi. The case lo == hi is the single element, which counts when 2·nums[lo] ≤ target.
Computing 2 ** k directly. It overflows long before n = 100 000; keep a modded table.
Counting distinct values instead of positions. [2, 2, 2] has 7 valid subsequences, not 1.

solutions.title: Try every subset
solutions.idea: Enumerate all 2^n − 1 non-empty subsets with a bitmask and test min + max.

solutions.title: Sort + two pointers
solutions.idea: Fix the minimum with the left pointer; the right pointer marks the largest allowed partner. Everything in between is free: 2^(hi − lo) subsets.

followups: Count subsequences with min + max exactly equal to target. What changes?
Why is sorting allowed here when the problem talks about subsequences, which normally keep order?
